accepted.s: Who co-authored the book *Target 3 Billion*, in which the PURA concept was elaborated?
accepted.x: Srijan Pal Singh co-authored *Target 3 Billion* with Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, in which the PURA concept was elaborated.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact person associated with a book rather than the originator of the concept.
accepted.sec: PURA and Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission - proponent, objective, launch, funding

accepted.s: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission is best described as:
o: A successor and expansion of the PURA approach
A special programme for urban slum redevelopment
A scheme exclusively for tribal hostels
A replacement for the National Extension Service
accepted.x: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission, launched in 2016, is the successor and expansion of the PURA approach.
accepted.tq: Use the successor–predecessor relationship to distinguish closely related rural development initiatives.
accepted.sec: PURA and Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission - proponent, objective, launch, funding

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission:
1. It seeks to develop more than 300 Rurban clusters.
2. It aims to preserve the rural soul while providing urban amenities.
3. One of its objectives is to curb distress migration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The mission envisages more than 300 Rurban clusters, combines the rural soul with urban amenities, and seeks to reduce distress migration.
accepted.tq: Test a mission through its scale, distinctive approach and intended social effect.
accepted.sec: PURA and Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission - proponent, objective, launch, funding

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission?
o: Replacing all Gram Panchayats with urban local bodies
accepted.x: The mission aims to stimulate local economic development, enhance basic services and create well-planned clusters. It does not replace Gram Panchayats with urban local bodies.
accepted.tq: Find the option that exceeds the institutional scope of the mission.
accepted.sec: PURA and Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission - proponent, objective, launch, funding

accepted.s: A Rurban cluster in a plain or coastal area normally comprises contiguous villages having a population of:
accepted.x: For plain and coastal areas, a Rurban cluster comprises contiguous villages with a population of 25,000 to 50,000.
accepted.tq: Separate population norms by geographical category before selecting the range.
accepted.sec: PURA and Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission - proponent, objective, launch, funding

accepted.s: For desert, hilly and tribal areas, a Rurban cluster is defined as contiguous villages having a population of:
accepted.x: In desert, hilly and tribal areas, the prescribed population range for a Rurban cluster is 5,000 to 25,000.
accepted.tq: Apply the geographical exception to the general cluster population norm.
accepted.sec: PURA and Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission - proponent, objective, launch, funding

accepted.s: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission was launched on 21 February 2016 at:
accepted.x: The mission was launched on 21 February 2016 at Kurubhat in Rajnandgaon district of Chhattisgarh.
accepted.tq: Combine the date with the precise launch location to avoid district–state swaps.
accepted.sec: PURA and Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission - proponent, objective, launch, funding

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the funding pattern of the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission?
o: It is funded mainly through convergence of existing schemes, with Critical Gap Funding up to 30% of project cost.
It is funded only by the concerned State Government through a 90:10 formula.
It is financed through foreign assistance without any scheme convergence.
It is financed entirely through a dedicated Central grant.
accepted.x: The mission mainly uses convergence of existing schemes and provides Critical Gap Funding of up to 30% of project cost.
accepted.tq: Distinguish convergence-based financing from a wholly dedicated grant mechanism.
accepted.sec: PURA and Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission - proponent, objective, launch, funding

accepted.s: Under the general funding pattern of the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission, the Centre–State sharing ratio is:
accepted.x: The normal Centre–State funding ratio is 60:40. A 90:10 ratio applies to North-Eastern and Himalayan States.
accepted.tq: Remember the general ratio separately from the special-region ratio.
accepted.sec: PURA and Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission - proponent, objective, launch, funding

accepted.s: In the North-Eastern and Himalayan States, the Centre–State sharing ratio under the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission is:
accepted.x: The Centre–State sharing ratio is 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States, compared with 60:40 in other States.
accepted.tq: Test the special funding exception rather than the general rule.
accepted.sec: PURA and Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission - proponent, objective, launch, funding

accepted.s: How many panchayats in Andhra Pradesh were classified by the Ministry of Rural Development under Rurban clusters?
accepted.x: The Ministry of Rural Development classified 359 panchayats in Andhra Pradesh under Rurban clusters.
accepted.tq: Use the state-specific quantitative figure as the distinguishing fact.
accepted.sec: PURA and Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission - proponent, objective, launch, funding

accepted.s: Which institution conducts an annual Gram Panchayat-level ranking survey as part of its rural development framework?
accepted.x: Mission Antyodaya includes an annual Gram Panchayat-level ranking survey and functions as a convergence framework for rural development.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive administrative activity with the institution performing it.
accepted.sec: Rural development institutions and missions → objective

accepted.s: CAPART is primarily associated with:
o: Funding voluntary organisations and promoting rural technology
Providing modern inputs only to desert farmers
accepted.x: CAPART, or the Council for Advancement of People's Action and Rural Technology, funds voluntary organisations and supports rural technology.
accepted.tq: Expand the acronym and connect it with its core institutional function.
accepted.sec: Rural development institutions and missions → objective

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. CAPART was established in 1986.
2. CAPART functions under the Ministry of Rural Development.
3. CAPART is primarily responsible for conducting the Gram Panchayat ranking survey under Mission Antyodaya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: CAPART was established in 1986 and is associated with the Ministry of Rural Development. The Gram Panchayat ranking survey belongs to Mission Antyodaya, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that assigns one institution's distinctive function to another.
accepted.sec: Rural development institutions and missions → objective

accepted.s: The District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) served as the district-level organ for implementing:
o: Only urban housing programmes under the Ministry of Housing
Ministry of Rural Development anti-poverty programmes, beginning with IRDP
Forest conservation programmes under the Ministry of Environment
accepted.x: DRDA was the district organ responsible for implementing Ministry of Rural Development anti-poverty programmes, beginning with IRDP.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct implementing agency by matching its level and programme domain.
accepted.sec: Rural development institutions and missions → objective

accepted.s: The principal objective of ITDA/TADP is to:
o: Raise agricultural output through modern inputs, horticulture and fruit plantations, while supporting tribal livelihoods
Provide only urban amenities to selected villages
Construct national highways in tribal districts
Promote industrial exports from metropolitan regions
accepted.x: ITDA and TADP seek to improve agricultural output through modern inputs, horticulture and fruit plantations and to strengthen tribal livelihoods.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete objective rather than a narrow fragment.
accepted.sec: Rural development institutions and missions → objective

accepted.s: TADP is associated with the Tribal Sub-Plan introduced during the:
accepted.x: The Tribal Area Development Programme is associated with the Tribal Sub-Plan of the Fifth Five-Year Plan.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between adjacent Five-Year Plan periods.
accepted.sec: Rural development institutions and missions → objective

accepted.s: Which department became a separate Ministry in 2011 and, since June 2019, has been a Department under the Ministry of Jal Shakti?
accepted.x: Drinking Water and Sanitation became a separate Ministry in 2011 and has been a Department under the Ministry of Jal Shakti since June 2019.
accepted.tq: Track an institutional change through its two successive administrative stages.
accepted.sec: Rural development institutions and missions → objective

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. SGSY
B. Community Development Programme
C. Bharat Nirman
D. Food for Work
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Community Development Programme (1952), Food for Work (1977–78), SGSY (1999), and Bharat Nirman (2005).
accepted.tq: Place the earliest and latest programmes first, then resolve the middle sequence by year.
accepted.sec: Evolution of rural development programmes - chronology

accepted.s: Which programme was launched in 1953 as the immediate successor in the chronology of early rural development efforts after the Community Development Programme?
accepted.x: The National Extension Service was launched in 1953, after the Community Development Programme of 1952.
accepted.tq: Use a close-year chronology question to distinguish early rural programmes.
accepted.sec: Evolution of rural development programmes - chronology

accepted.s: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee, which reviewed the Community Development Programme and National Extension Service, submitted its report in:
accepted.x: The Balwantrai Mehta Committee reviewed the Community Development Programme and National Extension Service and submitted its report in November 1957.
accepted.tq: Pair the committee with both its subject of review and its exact reporting year.
accepted.sec: Evolution of rural development programmes - chronology

accepted.s: TRYSEM, launched in 1979, stands for:
o: Training Rural Youth for Social and Economic Management
Technology for Rural Youth and Small Employment
Targeted Rural Youth Scheme for Employment Mobilisation
accepted.x: TRYSEM stands for Training Rural Youth for Self-Employment and was launched in 1979.
accepted.tq: Test the exact expansion of a similar-looking rural employment acronym.
accepted.sec: Evolution of rural development programmes - chronology

accepted.s: SGSY, introduced in 1999, was formed by merging IRDP, TRYSEM, DWCRA and other programmes. The correct expansion of SGSY is:
accepted.x: SGSY stands for Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana. It was introduced in 1999 through the merger of several earlier programmes.
accepted.tq: Use the merger history to identify the exact scheme name and expansion.
accepted.sec: Evolution of rural development programmes - chronology

accepted.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
o: PMGSY — 25 December 2000 — Ministry of Rural Development
Jal Jeevan Mission — 15 August 2019 — Ministry of Rural Development
Vibrant Villages Programme — 2022–23 — Ministry of Rural Development
accepted.x: PMGSY was launched on 25 December 2000 under the Ministry of Rural Development. PMAY-G is under Rural Development, Jal Jeevan Mission under Jal Shakti, and the Vibrant Villages Programme under Home Affairs.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure launch-date and ministry pair, then eliminate ministry swaps.
accepted.sec: Scheme → launch, ministry, target

accepted.s: PMAY-G is intended to provide:
o: Solid waste processing facilities in urban areas only
Tap water to every rural household
Pucca houses with basic amenities in rural areas
accepted.x: PMAY-G targets the provision of pucca houses with basic amenities to eligible rural households.
accepted.tq: Separate housing, tap-water, road-connectivity and sanitation objectives.
accepted.sec: Scheme → launch, ministry, target

accepted.s: The target of the Jal Jeevan Mission is to provide:
o: Tap water to every rural household
Employment to one member of every rural household
A pucca house to every rural family
accepted.x: The Jal Jeevan Mission seeks to provide tap water to every rural household.
accepted.tq: Identify the scheme by its precise service-delivery target.
accepted.sec: Scheme → launch, ministry, target

accepted.s: The objective of ODF Plus under SBM-Gramin Phase II is to:
o: Provide only individual household toilets in urban areas
Provide pucca houses in difficult terrain
Sustain open-defecation-free status and undertake solid and liquid waste management
accepted.x: SBM-Gramin Phase II focuses on sustaining ODF status and managing solid and liquid waste, together described as ODF Plus.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the second-phase qualitative objective from the original sanitation drive.
accepted.sec: Scheme → launch, ministry, target

accepted.s: SBM-Gramin Phase II was approved in 2020 for implementation up to:
accepted.x: SBM-Gramin Phase II was approved in 2020 and was to continue up to 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Match the approval year with the stated implementation end period.
accepted.sec: Scheme → launch, ministry, target

accepted.s: The Drought-Prone Area Programme (DPAP) and Desert Development Programme (DDP) were launched, respectively, in:
accepted.x: DPAP was launched in 1973–74, while DDP was launched in 1977–78.
accepted.tq: Distinguish two similarly named programmes through their launch sequence and years.
accepted.sec: Scheme → launch, ministry, target

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the targets of DPAP and DDP?
o: DPAP targets border villages, while DDP targets rural housing.
DPAP addresses drought-prone areas, while DDP addresses hot and cold desert areas.
DPAP addresses deserts, while DDP addresses drought-prone areas.
Both programmes exclusively target urban infrastructure.
accepted.x: DPAP focuses on drought-prone areas, whereas DDP covers hot and cold desert areas.
accepted.tq: Split the options by comparing the target area of two confusable programmes.
accepted.sec: Scheme → launch, ministry, target

accepted.s: The Vibrant Villages Programme, announced in the Budget 2022–23, is administered by the:
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
accepted.x: The Vibrant Villages Programme was announced in Budget 2022–23 under the Ministry of Home Affairs and targets villages on the northern border.
accepted.tq: Apply the ministry-swap trap to a border-area development programme.
accepted.sec: Scheme → launch, ministry, target

accepted.s: The population norm for an eligible unconnected habitation under PMGSY is correctly stated as:
o: 250 or more in plains and 500 or more in all hilly areas
1,000 or more in plains and 500 or more in tribal areas
500 or more in plains and 250 or more in hill States, North-Eastern States, deserts and Schedule V areas
100 or more in plains and 250 or more in all other areas
accepted.x: PMGSY generally covers habitations with 500 or more population in plains and 250 or more in hill States, the North-East, deserts and Schedule V or tribal areas.
accepted.tq: Compare the general population threshold with the special-area relaxation.
accepted.sec: PMGSY - objective, connectivity norms, phases

accepted.s: In Left-Wing Extremism-affected blocks, PMGSY applies to eligible habitations having a population of:
accepted.x: In Left-Wing Extremism-affected blocks, the applicable population threshold is 100 or more.
accepted.tq: Identify the special exception to the standard PMGSY population norms.
accepted.sec: PMGSY - objective, connectivity norms, phases

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly matches the phases of PMGSY?
o: PMGSY-I—2000—new connectivity; PMGSY-II—2013—upgradation; PMGSY-III—2019—through routes and major rural links
accepted.x: PMGSY-I began in 2000, PMGSY-II in 2013 focused on upgradation, and PMGSY-III began in 2019 for through routes and major rural links.
accepted.tq: Start from the phase years and verify each phase's distinctive function.
accepted.sec: PMGSY - objective, connectivity norms, phases

accepted.s: The RCPLWEA component of the rural road programme was introduced in:
accepted.x: RCPLWEA was introduced in 2016 for the construction of roads in Left-Wing Extremism-affected areas.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the special LWE-road component from the numbered PMGSY phases.
accepted.sec: PMGSY - objective, connectivity norms, phases

accepted.s: According to the stated assessment, PMGSY has connected what percentage of targeted eligible areas?
accepted.x: PMGSY has connected 99.6% of the targeted eligible areas according to the stated assessment.
accepted.tq: Select the precise coverage figure rather than the absolute 100% distractor.
accepted.sec: PMGSY - objective, connectivity norms, phases

accepted.s: Under PMAY-G, the unit assistance for a house is correctly stated as:
o: Rs 1.00 lakh in plains and Rs 1.20 lakh in hilly areas
Rs 1.30 lakh in plains and Rs 1.50 lakh in hilly areas
Rs 1.50 lakh in plains and Rs 1.80 lakh in difficult terrain
Rs 1.20 lakh in plains and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly or difficult terrain
accepted.x: PMAY-G provides assistance of Rs 1.20 lakh per house in plain areas and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly or difficult terrain.
accepted.tq: Compare the standard unit assistance with the higher difficult-terrain amount.
accepted.sec: PMAY-G - unit assistance, beneficiary selection, target

accepted.s: Beneficiaries under PMAY-G are identified primarily on the basis of:
o: Annual income-tax returns verified by the District Collector
Voter-list data approved by the State Cabinet
SECC 2011 housing-deprivation data, verified by the Gram Sabha
Census 2001 occupational data, without local verification
accepted.x: PMAY-G beneficiaries are identified using housing-deprivation data from SECC 2011, followed by verification by the Gram Sabha.
accepted.tq: Identify both the data source and the required local verification authority.
accepted.sec: PMAY-G - unit assistance, beneficiary selection, target

accepted.s: By mid-2026, the number of rural houses completed under PMAY-G was reported as approximately:
accepted.x: The stated progress figure is 3.13 crore rural houses completed by mid-2026.
accepted.tq: Choose the precise current-progress figure while avoiding the older alternative count.
accepted.sec: PMAY-G - unit assistance, beneficiary selection, target
